title: Whelan v Halden Care (an invented matter)
about: A patient complains that an Irish company sends coded health records each night to a processor in the United States on standard contractual clauses. Four invented documents; real law, clause by clause. Whether the transfer is forbidden turns on from whose side 'personal data' is judged, and on whether the protection is in fact essentially equivalent.

Halden keeps the table linking study codes to patients
Meridian can work out who the patients are

arguments.text: Article 44 ends by requiring that the level of protection guaranteed by the Regulation is not undermined: data that are personal when they leave Dublin must be protected where they go
EDPS v SRB, paragraph 86: pseudonymised data are not personal data for a recipient who cannot identify the persons, so nothing personal reaches Meridian
Clause 14(a) speaks of the laws and practices of the destination: a law never applied to this importer does not prevent it from keeping the clauses
a protection that lasts only while the authorities choose not to ask is no guarantee of an essentially equivalent level of protection
